title: Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan sold 40% of its SpaceX stake after August lockup lifted
html:
SpaceX's mega rocket Starship lifts off for a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Nov. 13. Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan reported a 9.5-per-cent gain through the first half of the year, boosted by the increase in value of its SpaceX shares.Eric Gay/The Associated Press

Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan cashed in more than 40 per cent of its stake in Elon Musk’s SpaceX after the rocket and satellite company went public earlier this year, securing billions of dollars in gains from a modest early investment.

Teachers sold nearly 20.8 million shares in Space Exploration Technologies Corp. SPCX-Q, or roughly 41 per cent of its position in the company, between early August and the end of September, the pension plan’s regulatory filings show.

That reduced the Toronto-based pension fund’s stake in SpaceX from nearly 51 million shares as of June 30 – worth US$8.7-billion ($12.4-billion) at that time – to about 29.9 million shares worth US$4.5-billion ($6.4-billion) as of Sept. 30.

By unloading part of its stake, Teachers secured a major windfall from an early bet on SpaceX that has paid off handsomely. The Globe previously reported that Teachers invested about $300-million in the company in 2019 through its venture investing arm, and then made follow-on investments.

Teachers spokesperson Dan Madge declined to disclose the plan’s total proceeds from selling SpaceX shares.

The pension plan’s first opportunity to sell SpaceX stock was likely on Aug. 6, when the first of a series of staggered lockup restrictions expired. At that time, company shares were trading near their lowest level since its June 12 initial public offering, which sold a tranche of shares for US$135 each.

In an Aug. 10 interview, Teachers chief executive officer Jo Taylor said the plan had recently sold some shares but declined to disclose how many.

Even if Teachers sold all 20 million shares at the Aug. 6 closing price of US$114.92 on the Nasdaq, the plan’s gain would have been at least US$2.4-billion ($3.4-billion).

Since then, six further tranches of shareholder lockups have expired and SpaceX shares have mostly traded at higher prices, reaching a recent peak of US$171.92. If Teachers sold its shares at an average price at the midpoint of the stock’s price range over that span, its proceeds would be nearly US$3-billion ($4.3-billion).

Teachers’s SpaceX stake “has been a high-performing investment. Given the strong returns and the size of our position, we felt the time was right to sell a portion of our position and crystallize returns for our members,” Mr. Madge said in an e-mailed statement. “We remain confident about the company’s future prospects.”

Teachers manages $303.2-billion in assets on behalf of 346,000 working and retired members in Ontario. The plan reported a 9.5-per-cent gain through the first half of the year, boosted by the increase in value of its SpaceX shares.

The remaining SpaceX stake Teachers holds is still one of its largest individual investment positions. Mr. Taylor said in August, “Over time we’re going to have to look at that position and say, ‘What is the right size for the portfolio?’”

The plan must find a balance between avoiding overexposure to the moonshot company controlled by the mercurial Mr. Musk, while maintaining a chance to capitalize on future gains if the company’s value skyrockets again.

SpaceX is discussing a possible merger with Tesla Inc., the electric-car maker also led by Mr. Musk, in a potential blockbuster deal that would create a company with a multitrillion-dollar market value.

The expiry of lockup restrictions has made it possible to trade more SpaceX shares on the open market, helping support the company’s share price. The stock, which was worth US$137.36 per share when markets closed on Monday, is trading above its IPO price from June, but far below its all-time high of US$225.64.
summary: Fund secured billions of dollars in gains from a modest early investment that has paid off handsomely
